[p. 352]

**Surah al-Buruj**

Its purpose is to demonstrate the power to bring about the matter of rending asunder (*al-infiqaq*), which is the explicit subject of its ending: the granting of bliss to the friend (of God) and the punishment of the wretched one by means of the one who punished him in this world, someone whose punishment customarily could only come from God alone. This is a consolation to the hearts of the believers and a strengthening of them against the harm of the disbelievers, and [it demonstrates] the power of the One who encompasses everything in power and knowledge. (*al-Rahman*), the One who has encompassed the creatures with justice and forbearance; (*al-Rahim*), the One who has singled out His friends for the perfecting of His favour upon them, in actuality, as He has manifested it in record.

* *

When [the surah before it] concluded with the reward of the believer, the punishment of the disbeliever, and the mockery directed at him, after mentioning that He, glorified is He, knows best what the enemies conceal of deceit and what they intend of afflictions for the friends, and after threatening them with what they cannot withstand, and since they had tortured the believers with various kinds of torment, strived to tempt whoever among them they could overpower, and pressed upon them so severely that they forced them into the valley of Abu Talib and other "fortresses" (*buruj*) in the lands, and into separation from family and children, this surah begins with what He brought upon the people of tyranny (*al-jabarut*) [p. 353] from among those who came before them, in a manner that makes known that this infliction was certainly from Him, glorified is He, and makes known that those before them went beyond what these did, to being cast into the Fire, and that the people of faith remained steadfast. This is for the consolation and strengthening of the believers, and for the threatening and weakening and shattering of the disbelievers. So He said, swearing an oath on account of their denial and their conduct in persisting in enmity toward the party of God, [an oath] which demonstrates that God takes vengeance for them, and which shows the complete power to bring about the Resurrection:

﴿By the sky﴾, that is, the one exalted to the utmost height, firmly made to the utmost firmness, ﴿with its constellations﴾, that is, the mansions for the wandering planets, which God, exalted is He, has arranged in positions in which He placed in some the power of causing the causes of emergence and return through the growth of plants, in others the power of nurturing in the same way, and in the others the power of harvesting, through hidden causes which He, glorified is He, has established and which you do not see. However, because of your great familiarity with this, you come to perceive from it, through experience, matters that indicate complete power. Some of you attributed these to nature, due to the shortness of the view regarding the causes of causes and the weariness of thought in penetrating to the ultimate end that minds reach. Thus they exchanged gratitude for disbelief and took the signs as evidence for the opposite of what they indicate, because of the rigidity of the mind and the inversion of thought. What is meant by them are the twelve mansions:

[p. 354] Aries, Taurus, Gemini, Cancer, Leo, Virgo, Libra, Scorpio, Sagittarius, Capricorn, Aquarius, Pisces, through which the sun passes [in the year]. Or they are the twenty-eight (mansions) through which the moon passes in the month. These are the mansions of the sun, these twelve, by the moon's course, for each of which it spends two and a third days; that makes twenty-eight [days], and it remains hidden for two nights, and that is a month. This is an indication that the One who distinguished the sky with this detailed arrangement and subjected these stars in it for the benefit of mankind does not leave it aimless. Rather, there must be a recompense for what he does of good and evil. They were likened to palaces, because the wandering planets descend into them, and the fixed stars and great planets are in them. They were called *buruj* (constellations/towers) because of their prominence, or they are the gates of the sky, since the descents come out of them. The root of the word is for prominence.

Now the commentary, when this clause of the oath signifies the Resurrection, states it explicitly: ﴿And by the promised Day﴾, that is, the Day of Resurrection, the promise of which has been fulfilled, and it is established with a certainty that cannot be avoided, by what points to it from Our power in Our creatures, and that We have made for it causes which are ready with you while you do not see them and do not perceive any part of them, and the Messengers did not explain them to you because your intellects fall short of them, beyond the most of the indication by causes with which you are accustomed, like them, without difference. Except that it, although the intellect cannot independently comprehend it and does not understand from it anything beyond the heaven for the promise of it by the Messengers, yet does not reject it after hearing it.

When the gathering is for the purpose of presentation, and presentation necessarily involves witnesses, those witnessed against, and disputes over covenants, He said, declaring the vagueness to be for magnification and generalization, like ﴿The soul will know what it has presented﴾ [al-Takwir: 14], ﴿and a witness﴾, that is, a noble one from among the saints, ﴿and a witnessed one﴾, that is, the day itself is witnessed due to what it contains of tremendous signs and effects, or it is witnessed upon, for all creatures witness it, and there occurs in it of wonders matters that description falls short of. The witnessing prophets attend it, as do their nations, who are the ones witnessed against, and no small deed nor great deed is left except that it is counted. In this is the strongest warning to all servants.

When the answer to the oath [on -] is what the purpose of the surah and what precedes and follows it indicate, namely, "We will surely reward both groups, the allies and the enemies, and We will surely requite each one for what they did," He indicated this by their actions in this world, through some of the tyrants of the past and through what He does to the tyrants who denied the Prophet (ﷺ). He began with those who are punished by Allah's punishment on the Day of Resurrection, to start with them at the end of Surah al-Inshiqaq, by the oath of the deniers, who are the ones spoken of. He expressed this in a way suited to supplication, while the reality is consolation for the believers, strengthening them with what happened to people like them, and a warning against what befell their kind. ﴿Cursed be﴾, that is, a curse, with the easiest and simplest matter (p. 356) from every one who curses, a curse with no success accompanying it. In this world it actually happened that ﴿the people of the trench﴾ were killed, that is, the great ditch, which is a long cleft in the earth like a river. It is narrated that a king of the disbelievers, and it is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him both) that he was from Himyar, one of the kings of Yemen, who lived seventy years before the birth of the Prophet (ﷺ), and many people believed in his time. He dug a trench in the earth for them and set it ablaze with fire, and he presented those who believed before it. Whoever turned back from his religion, he left alone, and whoever remained firm, and they were the majority, he threw into that trench and burned.

Abu Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr said: This surah came in the context of the iltifat (a shift in grammatical address, turning from one mode of speech to another) and the 'udul (a turning away, a change of direction) toward informing the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) about what this surah contains of the story of the people of the trench. This type of discourse has already occurred in Surah al-Mujadila and Surah al-Naba', and we have explained its occurrence in the very core and texts of the surahs, and it is closer and clearer between the two surahs. End.

When He, glorified and exalted, censured them, He explained the reason for their censure by making ﴿the fire﴾ a substitute of inclusion for "the trenches" (al-ukhdud). So He said: ﴿The fire﴾, that is, the great one which they prepared for the torment of Our friends. He increased its magnitude by His saying ﴿full of fuel﴾, that is, the thing with which it is kindled, from all that is suitable for that, of firewood and other things. And he attached to "was killed" (qatala) His saying:

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 85, verse 6:

﴿When they were sitting by it﴾ — that is, with their outward forms and their inner selves, ﴿by it﴾ — that is, upon the edges of its trench (p-357) ﴿sitting﴾ — that is, guarding it, and carrying out what their king commands them concerning its affair, such as casting the people [into it] and other things, acting like one who sits at ease, with no occupation other than it.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 85, verse 7:

﴿And they, over what they were doing﴾, i.e., specifically, through the strength of their motives toward doing it and their desire for it, from the trial by exposing (the believers) to the Fire and other things, repeating that act. ﴿Against the believers﴾, i.e., those firmly established in faith, whom the punishment did not turn away from it. ﴿Witnesses﴾, i.e., some of them testify for others before the King that he (the believer) did not fall short in what he was commanded to do. And they will testify on the Day of Resurrection to what their hands and feet bear witness against them concerning themselves for this wrongdoing, and some of them will bear witness against others, and each of them will oppose the others and shift (blame) onto the other, out of hope for salvation.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 85, verse 8:

Since this grave act could not come from a rational person except for a reason befitting it, he made clear that it was only for a cause far removed from such conduct, so he said, in the manner of the poet:

"There is no fault in them, except that their swords, by them, are notched from the clashing of the battalions."

﴿And they did not resent﴾, i.e., they did not disapprove of and dislike ﴿from them﴾, from the conditions, though it was their religion and a flaw in their eyes, ﴿except that they believe﴾, i.e., renew their faith while remaining steadfast in it, ﴿in Allah﴾, i.e., the King, the Most High, who possesses all attributes of perfection.

Since it might have been thought that His (glorified is He) leaving them unpunished, because they were torturing those who believed in Him for their belief, was improper, He negated that with His saying, describing Himself with what establishes the obligation of worship to Him and His being singled out for it: ﴿the Mighty﴾, i.e., the One who overcomes whoever He wills and is not overcome by anything, so it is not supposed that He is unable to act toward those who are under His guardianship out of incapacity; rather He tests them so as to magnify their rewards, to magnify the punishment of their enemies, and to magnify the retribution against them; ﴿the Praiseworthy﴾, i.e., the one encompassing all attributes of perfection, so He rewards whoever is afflicted for His sake with the greatest reward, and takes vengeance upon whoever harmed him with the most severe punishment. He established this with His saying:

﴿Who* alone* possesses the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾, meaning in a general sense, without restriction. Everything in them is therefore worthy that He alone be worshipped and that nothing be associated with Him.

When He (glorified is He) had preceded the warning with the witness and the witnessed, and with the fact that the disbelievers are witnesses against themselves, He increased the warning by stating that He (glorified is He) is [the greatest -] witness on that Day and on others. He does not need anyone else. However, He expressed this in the manner we are accustomed to, so He said: ﴿And Allah﴾ [i.e. -] the Greatest King, who has complete encompassing knowledge, ﴿is over all things﴾, i.e. this act and other than it, ﴿a witness﴾, i.e. a witness in the most perfect sense, from whom nothing is absent at all, and nothing exists or remains except by His management. One who has these great attributes does not neglect His allies at all; rather, He must (p-359) take vengeance on their enemies for them and exalt them with His loftiness. For this reason He said, beginning a new statement as an answer to one who says, "What did He do to them?", emphasizing the disbelievers' denial of that:

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 85, verse 10:

﴿Indeed, those who persecuted﴾ meaning: they mixed in harm with what their strength cannot bear, so that they must incline (to the truth) or turn away, at whatever time and from whatever people they may be, ﴿the believing men and the believing women﴾ meaning: those firmly established in the attribute of faith.

And since repentance is accepted before the death rattle (al-gharghara), however long the time, he expressed it with the particle of delay, saying: ﴿then they did not repent﴾ meaning: from their sins and their disbelief. And since He, glorified is He, does not punish anyone except for a cause, He made the cause of their sin and their not repenting his saying: ﴿then for them﴾ meaning: specifically, because of their disbelief, ﴿is the punishment of Hell﴾ meaning: the level into which they will be cast, with the utmost hatred and sullenness; this is in the Hereafter. ﴿And for them﴾ meaning: in addition to that, in both abodes, because of their persecution of the friends of Allah, ﴿is the punishment of the Burning﴾ meaning: the punishment whose nature is to exaggerate in burning, for what they burned of the hearts of the friends (of Allah). He, glorified is He, has indeed fulfilled this his saying regarding those who denied the Prophet ﷺ, by destroying them with the worst destruction, defeated and subdued, even though they had been certain that they were victorious, as He did with those before them. This shows that He is powerful over everything, and it shows that He originates and restores (creation).

(p-360) When He had mentioned the punishment of the obstinate deniers, beginning with it because the context calls for it, He followed it with the reward of the worshippers, saying, emphasizing against their enemies' denial of this: ﴿Indeed, those who believed﴾, that is, who professed faith, even at the lowest degree, from among those thrown into the fire and others, from every group in every time, ﴿and did righteous deeds﴾, confirming their faith and verifying it. Since Allah, glorified is He, in His mercy had already covered His friends with His care and did not leave them to their deeds, He did not make their deeds the cause of their happiness; so He did not connect His statement ﴿for them﴾ with the particle of consequence (fa'), that is, as the recompense for their enduring the fires of this world, from the material fire of the Trench that was mentioned, and from the fires of grief and sorrow that are inward, whose immediate cause is other than Him, glorified is He, so that the one who suffers them, while preserving his religion, is like one who grasps a live coal. ﴿Gardens﴾, that is, as a bounty from Him, ﴿beneath which rivers flow﴾. He brought their attainment close by the use of the preposition, saying: ﴿beneath them﴾, that is, beneath their upper chambers, their couches, and all their places, ﴿the rivers﴾, enjoying their coolness in exchange for that heat which they endured in the world, and the sight of them delights them, along with the greenness of the gardens and the beautiful faces, which bring joy and dispel sorrows.

When He had mentioned this which gladdens the souls and removes misery, He summed it up by His saying: ﴿That﴾, that is, the matter of lofty rank and great blessing, ﴿is the great triumph﴾ (p-361), that is, the attainment of all desired things and nothing else, ﴿the great﴾, with a greatness such that you do not comprehend from it more than what the one who described it with this attribute indicated in summary. The reason for its greatness is that this entire existence is smaller than the smallest thing in it.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 85, verse 12:

Since He rewards and punishes in this manner only one who is at the utmost degree of greatness, He stated, giving the reason for His act and thereby indicating by this reasoning His greatness, which thoughts fall short of reaching, and emphasizing against the denial of the enemies: ﴿Indeed, the seizure of your Lord﴾, i.e., the seizing of the One who does good to you, who manages your affair, of the enemies of the religion, with violence, dominance and utmost severity, ﴿is severe﴾, i.e., a severity whose harshness exceeds the violence inherent in the meaning of seizing (baṭsh), which is required for its being so named; so it is a doubled violence.

Since this violent seizing (al-baṭsh) can only be carried out by one whose power is complete, He indicated the completeness of His power and His exclusive possession of it by saying, emphasizing against their denial: ﴿Indeed, He﴾. He added further emphasis with another subject, to indicate exclusivity, saying: ﴿He﴾, that is, alone, ﴿originates﴾ (yubdi'), that is, brings into existence from nothing, whatever creation He wills, in whatever form He wills, ﴿and repeats﴾ (yu'īd), that is, returns that created being after its annihilation, at whatever time He wills. No other can do any of this.

This pronoun is not a separator (ḍamīr faṣl), because a separator pronoun occurs only when the predicate is definite, or resembles the definite in that the definite article *al-* (ʼal) cannot attach to it, as in *khayrun minka* (better than you). Al-Mazini permitted its occurrence before the present tense (al-muḍāriʻ), since the present tense resembles the noun and cannot take *al-*, so it resembles the definite. He said: it cannot occur before the past tense (al-māḍī), because the past tense does not resemble the noun. Al-Radi said: what he said is an assertion without proof. The verse *"wa-makru ulāʼika huwa yabūr"* (And the plotting of those—it will perish) is not a clear text that it is a separator, since it is permissible for it to be the subject with what follows it as its predicate. He refuted his statement about the past tense with the words of the Exalted: ﴿And that it is He who causes laughter and weeping﴾ [al-Najm: 43], and the rest of the verse.

When He, glorified be He, mentioned His seizing (*baṭsh*), and the one capable of severity may not be capable of gentleness, and even if he is capable of it, he may not be able [to attain] its full extent (*al-iblagh*), and He could not erase sins, their essences and their traces, for everyone in such a way that the sinner receives no punishment or reproach from anyone at all, except for the one who is capable of everything, He said, explaining all of that as evidence that He is the Doer who chooses, and emphasizing His transcendence beyond customary patterns: ﴿And He﴾, that is, He alone, ﴿is the Forgiving﴾, that is, the One who erases the essences of sins and their traces when He wills, in such a way that the one whose sin He erases experiences no distress at all from that sin. ﴿The Loving﴾, that is, the One who treats whoever He wills as a very loving friend does: He responds to them in whatever they ask, casts upon the sinner whose sin He has erased a love (*wudd*), meaning a great and wide affection, and places mercy for him in the hearts of creation. The root *w-d-d* revolves around expansiveness, as I have explained in Surat al-Rum. He added emphasis to the matter by mentioning what (p-363) is not disputed at all as being exclusively His, honoring Him and drawing attention to the fact that He is the greatest of created beings.

Dhu al-'Arsh (the Owner of the Throne): that is, the Owner of the greatest might, or the throne that indicates His exclusive kingship, His sole governance, management, lordship and direction of affairs, by which the matters of all things are sustained. Al-Majid (the Glorious): that is, the Noble, the Generous, the Great in His essence and attributes, the Good and Beautiful, the Exalted and Lofty, the Abundant in giving. This is when it is read in the nominative, as an attribute of "Dhu" (dhu). It is likewise when it is read in the genitive, as an attribute of "al-'Arsh," in the recitation of Hamzah and al-Kisa'i.

Since specificity (al-ikhtisas) certainly indicates perfection of power, mention of these specifications produced His saying: ﴿Doer (fa''al) of whatever He wills﴾, that is, by way of repetition and emphasis. ﴿Of whatever He wills﴾ — no act is burdensome to Him, whether the acts are attributed to Him directly without intermediary or are, in appearance, attributed to others.

When the proof that His seizing is severe had been completed, He established it by what was found of that and reminded him of it, as a warning and a consolation to him, because consideration of perceptible things is more effective upon souls. So He said: ﴿Has there come to you﴾, that is, O greatest of Our creation, ﴿the report of the hosts﴾, that is, recall what has come to you of what befell them of Our seizing and what fell upon them of Our might, because of their denial of Our messengers, upon them be the best of prayers and peace, to the extent that it became a report recited and a remembrance among creation for its greatness that does not fade. The word "al-junud" (the hosts) is the plural of "jund" with a damma, and it is the army prepared for fighting, and the helpers, and the city. All of them point to great valor and excessive dominance.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 85, verse 18:

Since it is known from the context that what is meant by their account (ḥadīth) is what befell them of seizure (baṭsh) for denying the Messengers, especially regarding the Resurrection to which the context relates, and since the clearest of the signs demonstrated through the signs of Moses and Ṣāliḥ, upon both of them be prayer and peace, were more evident than what occurred through the signs of others who came before them in time, and since the nation of every Prophet among the Prophets and the followers of Pharaoh contained many kinds of creatures, it is related that the vanguard of Pharaoh on the day he pursued the Children of Israel and was drowned numbered six hundred thousand. He (God) substituted "Pharaoh" (Fir'awn) for "the armies" (al-junūd), to make known that they were the enemies of God. Likewise his followers, who were the most stubborn, most insolent and most foolish people of their time, and the most frivolous in claiming divinity for him and in affirming it. This was from the blindness of their hearts, together with the manifestness of the signs of lordship, both celestial and terrestrial, and their firmness in denial, folly, levity and recklessness, despite seeing those great signs in their multitude and their long duration, until he entered the sea secure from drowning, although the danger of drowning in that situation was not hidden from anyone possessing even a little of his intellect. So God drowned him and those with him, all of them, and left none of them. Therefore the curse of God be upon him and upon whoever was with him of his followers, and upon their followers, the Arab al-Ittiḥādiyya sect (the adherents of unity of existence), the followers of al-Fāriḍiyya, whose disbelief is made manifest by their approving of Pharaoh, on whose disbelief all sects have agreed. ﴿And Thamūd﴾, whose levity led them to hamstring the she-camel after seeing it emerge from the solid rock, not conceding that the One who broke custom by bringing it forth would destroy them on account of it. He, glorified is He, combined in these two (accounts) the Arabs and the non-Arabs, and destruction by water, which is the life of every thing, and the Cry (al-Ṣayḥa), which is the sign of the Hour. The signs of these two were clearer because the sign of Thamūd was a she-camel that came out of a solid rock. Among the signs of Moses, upon him be prayer and peace, was the creation of lice in mounds too numerous to count, likewise the creation of frogs and locusts, and the restoration of the staff to life a second time. No intelligent person doubts that One who is able to originate these things from something having no basis in life is even more powerful to restore to life what had been alive before.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 85, verse 19:

When the implied sense was: "Yes, [indeed] that has come to me, and I have known from their report and otherwise that You are capable of what You will, but [the disbelievers] do not believe me," He followed it with His words: ﴿Nay, those who disbelieved﴾, meaning: they openly declared disbelief, from these people and others, even though they are at the lowest rank, ﴿are in denial﴾, meaning: although they see the signs for which they have no basis of support, and it is a severe [denial] that encompasses them because they follow their desires and imitate their fathers. Thus they cannot escape that denial, which has become an enclosure for them after they heard the reports of these destroyed peoples and saw some of their traces, and after I set forth for them the proofs of resurrection in this inimitable Qur'an. Yet they took no lesson from any of that because of the disease of envy within them. So their condition is more astonishing than their [previous] condition, and He warned them of the like of their end.

Since this might give the impression that their denial was outside His intended purpose, glorified and exalted is He, He said, repelling that and emphasizing His power over seizing them, as a warning to them and a consolation to those who denied him: ﴿And Allah﴾, that is, while the fact is that the King, who is singled out for majesty and honor, ﴿from behind them﴾, that is, from every direction they conceal or that conceals them, and that is every direction, ﴿encompasses﴾ [so He encompasses] them from every direction by His knowledge and His power. It is a metaphor (kinayah) for their being in His grip, unable to escape Him in any way, just as one who falls into the grip of an enemy who surrounds him without any barrier cannot escape. He, glorified be He, is able to inflict upon them what He inflicted upon those (before them). Perhaps He specified "behind" (waraʾ) because a person protects what is behind him, and because it is the direction of flight from calamities.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 85, verse 21:

When their denial was at hand, and it was the greatest of their denials, they attacked the greatest of the Qur'an's signs by saying: "It is nothing but a fabrication, merely the fables of the ancients" (i.e., their own falsehoods, with no realities behind what it reports), even though it had itself established the greatest proof for itself, by itself, through its inimitability (i'jaz), showing that it is true. He spoke using the pronoun, signalling (iydhanan) that because of its greatness it is present in every heart, so that it has no absence at all, and there is no one who does not have a discourse concerning it. He built upon what its estimation implies: the matter is not as the disbelievers claim about the Qur'an: ﴿Nay, it is﴾, that is, this Qur'an, to which falsehood cannot come from before it or from behind it, a revelation from the All-Wise, the Praiseworthy, ﴿a Glorious Qur'an﴾, that is, one that gathers every noble excellence, reaching the highest summit in every nobility, ﴿Majid﴾, that is, honourable and generous, with nothing in it of the blemishes of reproach, mighty [great], noble, exalted, bountiful, of good qualities, unique in its composition and its meanings, both hidden and manifest, encompassing all the aspects of praise, not a created speech, nor is it created, but rather it is an attribute of the Creator; indeed it is bountiful in everything that is desired from it of goodness for whoever's intention is sincere, whose inner disposition is pure, whose aspiration is lofty and whose character is noble. Its glory therefore refuses that any criticism in any form should approach its precincts; and its glory is the testing of its judgments, among the swiftly witnessed and the later-known, by the world of what is witnessed. Thus it was known through certain experience, by what has been transmitted in successive reports of past narratives, what has been witnessed of present effects, and what continually renews over time of its like, its kinds and its forms. So he denied the one who said it is poetry, or soothsaying, or sorcery, or other than that of the falsehoods.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 85, verse 22:

When He described it (the Qur'an) in itself as something that rejects the attachment of any trace of doubt, by describing its station in the Highest Assembly (al-Mala' al-A'la), to inform that nothing befalls it that could alter it, He said: ﴿In a Preserved Tablet﴾ (p-368). The lawh is every broad sheet [of ] wood, bone, or other such material. ﴿Preserved﴾ means that it has preservation always, in the most perfect manner, from every flaw and from anyone reaching it except the noble angels. The Proof of Islam, al-Ghazali, may Allah have mercy on him, said in the Book of Death from the Ihya' (Revival of the Religious Sciences): "It is expressed sometimes as the Tablet (al-Lawh), sometimes as the Clear Book (al-Kitab al-Mubin), and sometimes as the Clear Imam (Imam Mubin). It gathers what has occurred in the world and what will occur, written in it as books that are not witnessed with this eye, and it is not of the kind of tablets we are accustomed to. His Tablet, may He be exalted, does not resemble the tablets of His creation, just as His Essence, may He be exalted, does not resemble the essences of His creation. Its likeness is the likeness of the heart of a human in memorizing the Qur'an, for example its words and letters; if one searched his heart, nothing would be found in it, and only a prophet or a saint near to his rank can perceive that." This is the meaning of the words of the Imam, may Allah have mercy on him.

Nafi' read ﴿Majid﴾ with a raised ending (ḍamma) as an attribute of the Qur'an, so that it preserves it from alteration, distortion, falsification, and every doubt and suspicion in its composition or its meaning, just as the constellations (al-Buruj) are preserved in the Preserved Celestial Tablet. Rather, the Qur'an is more deserving of this, because it is the attribute of the Creator in clarifying His description of what He created in the most perfect and most just manner, since it is the translation of what Allah, glory be to Him, brought into existence. Thus it is certainly true that it must be truthful in all that it reports. Among the greatest of these is that He, glory be to Him, will gather people for the Judgment (al-Dayunah) with reward and punishment, just as they repaid His friends in this world [with] denial, (p-369) with the like of that. So He seized His enemies and saved His friends. Thus the conclusion returns to the beginning, and the opening embraces the end. This requires the exaltation of the Speaker [of it] above leaving anything, let alone souls, without preservation, and above everything that is unbecoming, and the affirmation for Him of perfections and greater perfections in every way. And Allah knows best what is correct, and to Him is the return and the final place, and to Him is the refuge and the turning.
